purpose: Independent human annotation of directly observable answer behavior for a future Face-Fit pilot; levels are rubric labels and are not automated scores or thresholds.

anchors.LEVEL_1: Large, repeated orientation changes interrupt visual continuity.
anchors.LEVEL_2: Several orientation changes are visible and occasionally interrupt continuity.
anchors.LEVEL_3: Minor changes occur without sustained disruption.
anchors.LEVEL_4: Orientation remains visually steady with only task-relevant movement.

notObservableWhen: Face is absent or occluded for most of the answer.
insufficientDataWhen: The observable segment is too brief.
Video decoding or landmark availability is materially incomplete.
raterNotes: Rate head orientation only, never eye contact or attention.
items.operationalDefinition: Rate only the directly visible or audible behavior described by the anchors; do not derive the label from an automated metric value.
items.observationWindow: Complete answer, excluding intervals marked unavailable or invalid.
items.inclusionRule: Include an event only when the relevant modality is directly observable and temporally attributable to the answer.
items.exclusionRule: Exclude capture failures, camera motion, interruptions, and events outside the answer; use a special status when exclusion prevents judgment.
examples: Minor changes occur without sustained disruption.
Orientation remains visually steady with only task-relevant movement.
counterExamples: Large, repeated orientation changes interrupt visual continuity.
Face is absent or occluded for most of the answer.

raterConfidence.rule: Record confidence separately from the rubric level; low confidence triggers review and never changes the level numerically.

limitations: Draft anchors require content review, rater training, and reliability testing.
The item cannot be used for automated or production scoring.

items.construct: Recovery after a visible head turn

anchors.LEVEL_1: Repeated turns remain displaced for extended portions.
anchors.LEVEL_2: Recovery is inconsistent after several turns.
anchors.LEVEL_3: Most turns return promptly to the prior orientation.
anchors.LEVEL_4: Turns are brief and recovery is consistently clear.

notObservableWhen: No visible turn occurs; use NOT_OBSERVABLE rather than assuming a high level.
Face is not visible during the relevant event.
insufficientDataWhen: Fewer than two interpretable events are available.
raterNotes: Do not infer where the eyes are looking.
Event absence is not evidence of a preferred behavior.
